data.headline: Spot the phish in sixty seconds

beats.say: Most attacks start with one email.
Here are three red flags, and one rule that beats them all.

header.label: Subject
header.text: URGENT: payment failed, act within 1 hour

data.title: Your account will be suspended
data.body: We could not process your last payment. Verify your card details now to avoid losing access to your account.

callouts.title: Lookalike domain
callouts.text: Ends in .co, not our real .com address.

callouts.title: False urgency
callouts.text: One hour deadlines are designed to rush you.

callouts.title: Asks for details
callouts.text: We never ask for card details by email.

beats.say: Here's a real looking email. Look at the sender first.
The domain ends in dot co, not our real dot com address.
Next, the false urgency. A one hour deadline is designed to rush you.
And it asks for your card details. We never do that by email.

data.label: That's all it takes to check a sender
data.sub: Ten seconds of checking is the cheapest security tool we have.

beats.say: Checking a sender takes about ten seconds.
It's the cheapest security tool we have.

data.headline: When in doubt
do: Report it with the Phish button

beats.say: When in doubt, report it with the phish button, and open the site yourself.
Don't click links in urgent emails, and never reply with any details.
So remember one rule: pause, check, then report.
Questions? Ask the security team any time.
